A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same attentive-probing study and EP method. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification benchmarks, efficiency comparisons, low-shot and layer-wise results, and attention analyses in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds PEFT comparisons, cross-dataset evaluation, localization, retrieval, and additional ablations.

M1.justification: The base EP pooling procedure remains unchanged. Section 4.2 adds a hybrid combining EP with LoRA adapters on value projections across backbone layers, and Appendix C.3 tests an auxiliary attention-similarity loss. These are extensions rather than a redesign of EP; the effective-query explanation restates the existing reparameterization.

E1.justification: The seven classification datasets are retained, but Appendix C.2 substantially expands task coverage: cross-dataset transfer among ImageNet-1K, StanfordCars, and Food101; object localization on ImageNet-1K; and zero-shot retrieval on CUB200 and Cars196. These introduce new task requirements and transfer scenarios using existing datasets.

E2.justification: v3 Figure 4 adds evaluated LoRA, BitFit, and LayerNorm-tuning comparators, extending the main comparison beyond pooling/probing methods. Appendix C also adds deeper AbMILP variants and LP with and without Matryoshka as controls. The original probing comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: The original 90-epoch classification protocol is retained. New experiments introduce LoRA layer/projection/rank sweeps, cross-dataset k-NN evaluation, WSOL MaxBoxAccV2 localization, full-dataset retrieval with every image serving as a query and Recall@1–32, and 10-versus-90-epoch checkpoint comparisons. These are added evaluation designs, not evidence that existing benchmarks were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds AbMILP depth ablations (Table 3), cross-dataset generalization analysis (Table 5), an intervention encouraging attention complementarity (Figure 13), convergence analysis (Table 9), and LP Matryoshka controls (Table 12). These test baseline selection, transfer, diversity, training efficiency, and dimensional truncation beyond v2's retained analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The retained standard-deviation visualizations summarize attention across heads, not experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 2 and the matched low-shot, layer-wise, attention-mixing, and EP Matryoshka results are retained. Substantial new results include LoRA+EP reaching 76.99% with 850K parameters, localization and retrieval scores, transfer results, and training analyses. These are additional configurations and evaluations, not same-setting improvements over v2. Results include exceptions: BEiTv2 Cars196 retrieval R@1 falls from 48.3 to 44.2 with EP.

T1.justification: The underlying equations, complexity arguments, and complementarity definitions are retained. The explicit effective-query identity clarifies algebra already present in v2. Likewise, adding lambda to the illustrative Matryoshka loss reflects weighting already described and evaluated there. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The systematic benchmark, efficient EP mechanism, and complementary-attention contributions remain central. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion add a claim that EP complements PEFT and that LoRA+EP improves accuracy–parameter trade-offs over either alone. Low-shot and layer-wise gains lose their explicit abstract emphasis, although their results remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations concerning EP's cross-dataset generalization relative to LoRA, diversity regularization accelerating convergence without improving final EP accuracy, and Matryoshka as exploratory rather than matching dimension-specific probes. It expands cached-feature trade-off discussion. However, some new retrieval and convergence generalizations exceed their tables, and Appendix D retains outdated statements about PEFT interaction and retrieval remaining future work.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page access pointer, explicitly identifies the default depth-1 AbMILP implementation, and documents LoRA target layers, projection matrices, ranks, and the transfer configuration. Retrieval dataset sizes and query construction are specified. Existing optimizer, learning-rate, batch-size, augmentation, and hardware information is retained; the PDF does not establish what resources the project page contains.

R1.justification: v3 adds the two Choe et al. localization-protocol references and develops EP's relationship to PEFT through explicit competition and complementarity claims. LoRA, BitFit, and LayerNorm tuning were already cited in v2. Most other reference changes update publication metadata rather than introduce different prior work.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten, the introduction and conclusion incorporate PEFT, and selected method and Matryoshka explanations are refined. The key/value ablation moves earlier within Section 4.3, while the overall section structure remains. Conference headers, acknowledgments, affiliation text, and bibliography formatting are also updated.

P2.justification: v3 adds the PEFT trade-off plot and auxiliary-loss learning curves, plus seven tables covering the new evaluations and controls. Figure 1 is redrawn with clearer labels, and Table 1 removes the separate vanilla-MHCA row while retaining its formulation in the text. Existing plots and attention visualizations are largely retained and relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 explicitly left PEFT synergy and applications beyond classification open. v3 substantially strengthens the paper by testing those questions through PEFT comparisons, hybrid configurations, transfer, localization, and retrieval, alongside useful controls. These gains outweigh localized reporting weaknesses: Table 8 contradicts uniformly positive retrieval wording, Table 9 shows MAE EP@10 at 60.0% versus LP@90 at 67.7%, and Appendix D was not reconciled with the added experiments.
